Weight gain from improved glycemic control is another com-
mon side eﬀ ect. Instead of losing glucose through urine, the 
body actually utilizes glucose or stores it as glycogen or fat.
Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA) Diabetic ketoacidosis 
(DKA), a severe form of hyperglycemia, is a life-threatening sit-
uation that commands prompt medical attention.36 DKA occurs 
more often in T1DM, but is also a risk for individuals with type 
2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) during acute illness and/or when 
they have become insulin deﬁ cient.37 Risk for DKA intensiﬁ es 
during illness, infection, and emotional stress. Omission of 
insulin is also a frequent cause. Individuals may not take their 
insulin when they feel too sick to eat, or because they are afraid 
of developing hypoglycemia.36, 37 Symptoms of DKA include 
nausea and/or vomiting; stomach pain; fruity or acetone breath; 
Kussmaul respirations; and mental status changes.37
